title: A friend to myself
hook: Hecaton says: I have begun to be a friend to myself

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was Hecaton, who saw hope and fear chained together like a prisoner and his guard. Your line was chained together.

You idiot, you forgot again. Why are you like this. Plenty of inner voices talk like that. Said out loud to a friend, those lines would cost the friendship. Inside a head, they can run for years. In his sixth letter, Seneca passes along another line from Hecaton: the answer he gave when someone asked how far he'd come.
screen: `YOU IDIOT. WHY ARE YOU LIKE THIS.` → `NEVER SAID TO A FRIEND.` → `A FRIEND TO MYSELF.`

segments.voice: Letter six opens with Seneca saying he feels himself not just improving but being transformed. He adds, honestly, that he still has much to correct, and that this is itself a sign of progress: you can finally see faults you couldn't see before. Then he shares what pleased him in Hecaton that day. Someone asks: what progress have you made? Hecaton answers, in Gummere's translation: I have begun to be a friend to myself. Not I've mastered my passions. Not I've read everything. Just that. Seneca calls this great progress, because such a person will never be alone. And someone who is a friend to himself, he adds, is a friend to everyone. The friendship starts at home and spreads outward. What kind of friend? Not flattery, or excusing everything. A few days ago Seneca told Lucilius to choose friends carefully and then trust them wholly. A good friend tells you the truth and stays on your side while doing it: honest about your faults, patient with them, never cruel. Be to yourself what a true friend would be. And notice the word begun. Even Hecaton was only starting.
screen: `SEEING FAULTS IS PROGRESS.` · `WHAT PROGRESS HAVE YOU MADE?` · `NEVER ALONE; A FRIEND TO ALL.` · `HONEST, PATIENT, NOT CRUEL.` · then, large: `A FRIEND TO MYSELF.`

segments.voice: Think of something you've been hard on yourself about lately, and hear the voice you've been using. Now imagine a good friend heard all of it, and let them answer, something honest and something kind at once. Then picture one small kindness for yourself, a glass of water, an early night, a real lunch, and let yourself be on your own side.
Hecaton, the Stoic Seneca quotes: his sign of progress was simply, I have begun to be a friend to myself. Today's word.
Your line: will never be alone. Honest, patient, and on your own side. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some who practice Stoicism measure progress not by perfection but by how they treat themselves: honest about faults, patient with them, and on their own side.
